issue: Notebook mixes widget handling, GitHub authentication, configuration, and orchestration of multiple other notebooks, violating the single‑responsibility principle.

suggested_refactor: Extract widget parsing, GitHub authentication, and configuration into separate helper modules (e.g., `widget_utils.py`, `github_auth.py`). Keep this notebook as a thin orchestrator that only calls those functions and `%run` the downstream notebooks.

issue: Three notebooks act as entry points, each performing widget extraction, GitHub authentication, and configuration loading before diverging to distinct processing steps, resulting in duplicated orchestration code.
why_it_matters: Duplicated entry‑point logic increases coupling and makes updates error‑prone; a change to the shared setup must be made in multiple places.
suggested_refactor: 1) Create a shared entry-point notebook (e.g., `RetentionMainNotebook`) that handles widget parsing, token retrieval (via the shared utility), and common configuration. 2) Move stage‑specific logic from `rawConfig_new_rules` and `new_tables_processor` into functions in separate modules (e.g., `raw_config_updater.py`, `new_tables_finder.py`). 3) Point all job definitions to the new shared entry‑point notebook. 4) Add a widget `stage` (or selector parameter) whose value determines which stage to execute; only when the value matches a specific stage does the flow continue on to the extra downstream steps. 5) Validate the selector value and fail loudly on unknown values.
